title: "CLI reference"
description: "Commands and flags validated against the current Cobra command tree."
---

This reference is validated against the Cobra command tree in `cmd/` and the
output of `go run . <command> --help`. `wraptool --help` remains authoritative
for the binary you have installed.

## Top level

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `wraptool` | In a Git repository, run `up` with defaults; outside one, show help |
| `wraptool serve` | Start the MCP server |
| `wraptool up` | Ensure the shared server and enter a project container |
| `wraptool down` | Stop or remove this worktree's Dev Container |
| `wraptool init` | Generate harness MCP configuration |
| `wraptool init devcontainer` | Scaffold a new Dev Container config |
| `wraptool harness` | Manage the version-locked harness pool |
| `wraptool requests` | Review capability requests |
| `wraptool server` | Inspect or stop the shared server |
| `wraptool config validate` | Strictly decode and validate configuration |
| `wraptool doctor` | Run the operator-facing preflight report |
| `wraptool version` | Print build version, revision, dirty state, and Go version |
| `wraptool completion` | Generate shell completion for bash, fish, PowerShell, or zsh |

`--version` prints the compact version. `version` prints the fuller build
identity.

## Server and container lifecycle

### `serve`

```text
wraptool serve [-c|--config PATH]
```

Config path precedence is flag, `WRAPTOOL_CONFIG`, then the XDG default. The
configured transport determines whether the process uses a TCP HTTP listener or a
Unix socket.

### `up`

```text
wraptool up [--config PATH] [--no-server] [--no-container]
            [--runtime auto|guix|devcontainer]
            [--shell auto|always|never] [--workspace PATH]
            [--harness NAME]
```

`--runtime` defaults to `auto`; it selects Guix only when `guix` is on `PATH`
and the worktree contains `manifest.scm`, otherwise Dev Container. `--harness`
defaults to `claude`. Orchestration currently requires `mcp.transport: sse`.

### `down`

```text
wraptool down [--workspace PATH] [--rm]
```

This finds a Dev Container by its workspace label. `--rm` removes it with force;
without the flag it is stopped. Guix containers are transient and are not
managed by `down`. The shared wraptool server remains running.

### `server`

```text
wraptool server status [-c|--config PATH]
wraptool server stop
```

`status` combines PID-file liveness with TCP reachability. `stop` sends SIGTERM
to the process recorded by the shared PID file.

## Client configuration

### `init`

```text
wraptool init --harness NAME[,NAME...] [--transport sse|unix]
              [--url URL] [--socket PATH] [--global] [--config PATH]
```

`--harness` is required and repeatable; comma-separated values and `all` are
accepted. Known names are `agy`, `claude`, `opencode`, and `pi`. Project output
is merged into each harness's JSON file when that file contains valid JSON.

::: {.callout-warning}
Unix client generation is incomplete: `--socket` does not create a bridge and
most listed harnesses expect an HTTP URL. Use an explicit bridge such as `socat`
or choose TCP.
:::

### `init devcontainer`

```text
wraptool init devcontainer [--harness claude|opencode|pi|agy]
  [--lang go,node,java,python,rust] [--base ubuntu|debian|alpine|IMAGE]
  [--out PATH] [--name NAME] [--force]
```

The command writes a new JSONC file and refuses to overwrite by default. npm
harnesses automatically add the Node feature. It is a scaffold, not a merger.

### `harness`

```text
wraptool harness list
wraptool harness install HARNESS [--constraint EXPR] [--backend auto|guix|oci]
                                 [--allow-young --reason TEXT]
wraptool harness refresh [HARNESS]
wraptool harness update [HARNESS] [--backend auto|guix|oci]
                                  [--allow-young --reason TEXT]
wraptool harness sync [HARNESS] [--platform KEY] [--backend auto|guix|oci]
wraptool harness rollback HARNESS [--to VERSION] [--platform KEY]
wraptool harness gc [--dry-run] [--legacy]
wraptool harness policy set [--harness NAME]
                            [--minimum-release-age DURATION]
                            [--minimum-observation-age DURATION]
                            [--allow-prereleases]
```

These commands manage harnesses in the developer
[harness pool](harness-pool.qmd), shared by every project. `claude`,
`opencode`, `pi`, and `agy` are locked and realized in the pool.

`manifest.yaml` records which harnesses you want and their version
constraints. `harness-lock.json` records the exact versions they resolved
to. A version moves through refresh (candidate metadata), resolve (the lock),
fetch (downloads), and realize (an offline-built generation). Activation
then points the pool at that generation.

| Command | Network | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `list` | none | Show each harness's constraint, locked, active, latest, and eligible versions, and remaining quarantine |
| `install` | yes | Record intent, then refresh, resolve, fetch, and realize; keeps an existing lock |
| `refresh` | metadata only | Record candidate versions in `observations.json`; no download, no lock change |
| `update` | yes | Lock the newest eligible candidate already refreshed, then fetch and realize it |
| `sync` | downloads only | Fetch missing or empty downloads for the current lock, then realize it; never resolves |
| `rollback` | none | Activate a previously realized generation; the lock is not changed |
| `gc` | none | Remove unreferenced generations, downloads, and staging directories |
| `policy set` | none | Edit quarantine and prerelease policy in `manifest.yaml`, keeping comments |

Without a `HARNESS` argument, `refresh` and `update` act on every harness in
`manifest.yaml`, and `sync` on every harness in the lock.

| Flag | Commands | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--constraint EXPR` | `install` | keep existing, else stable | Version constraint, such as `'>=2 <3'` or `'=2.1.220'` |
| `--backend` | `install`, `update`, `sync` | `auto` | `auto` uses Guix when it can build the target, else Docker or Podman |
| `--allow-young` | `install`, `update` | off | Bypass quarantine; requires `--reason`, which goes to the pool audit log |
| `--platform KEY` | `sync`, `rollback` | this host | `linux-amd64-glibc`, `linux-arm64-glibc`, `linux-amd64-musl`, or `linux-arm64-musl` |
| `--to VERSION` | `rollback` | newest other generation | Exact version to activate |
| `--dry-run` | `gc` | off | Report what would be removed |
| `--legacy` | `gc` | off | Also remove the pre-generation `bin/` and `lib/` trees; refused unless every harness is active |
| `--harness NAME` | `policy set` | pool-wide | Apply the policy to one harness |

`--backend guix` fails for a target architecture other than the host's.
`--backend oci` fails when neither `docker` nor `podman` is on `PATH`.

Each download prints its size, then progress every five seconds, on
stderr. An interrupted `install` or `update` reuses downloads that already
finished. `update` does not fetch when the lock is already current, so
use `sync` to repair a missing or empty download.

A later `sync`, `update`, or `install` can re-activate the lock's own
generation and undo a `rollback`.

## Requests and validation

```text
wraptool requests list [--status pending|approved|denied|""]
wraptool requests approve REQUEST_ID [--apply]
wraptool requests deny REQUEST_ID [--reason TEXT]
wraptool admin open [--print]
wraptool config validate [PATH]
wraptool config validate --config PATH
```

The default request-list filter is `pending`; an empty status displays all.
`admin open` opens the [review UI](web-ui.qmd) in the default browser, logged
in via its token; `--print` prints the login URL instead.
`approve --apply` first records approval, then attempts the atomic config edit.
If editing fails, request status remains approved while policy remains unchanged.

The positional config path and `--config` cannot be used together. Validation
strictly rejects unknown YAML keys and performs the same semantic checks used by
`serve`, without starting a server or wrapped tools.

## Diagnostics

### `doctor`

```text
wraptool doctor [-c|--config PATH] [--workspace DIR] [--json]
                [--only CHECK,...] [--skip CHECK,...] [--strict]
                [--no-probe] [--verify-pool]
```

An operator-facing preflight report: host dependencies, configuration
integrity, deployment posture, and policy content. Safe to run before any
configuration exists. Exit code `0` means no `fail` finding, `1` means at
least one, and `2` means doctor could not complete. See [wraptool
doctor](doctor.qmd) for the full report format, check groups, severity model,
and suppression syntax.
